known_limitations: Tiny synthetic transformers trained on all 144 task combinations rather than pretrained language models.
Workspace discovery uses supervised output-head semantics, analogous to a token lens but not open-ended semantic discovery.
The broader late space explains roughly 79 percent of residual variance and is not a tiny low-variance workspace.
PCA is essentially as effective as the Jacobian-informed construction on this benchmark.
The candidate state appears late and is reconstructible; persistent pair-level workspace closure is not established.
The full four-seed deterministic replay did not complete in the second execution attempt.
PyTorch is required but not vendored in the compact package.
No subjective-awareness, consciousness, sentience, valence, shared-mind, or moral-status claim.
The inherited uv.lock remains a v0.48 lock and was not used.
next_unclosed_gap: Instrument two small pretrained open-weight language models, estimate moving token-indexed J-lenses from actual residual streams during natural-language collaboration, and test whether cross-agent shared directions outperform PCA, survive task changes, and acquire recurrent pair-specific provenance.
principal_findings: The early recurrent average-Jacobian space had rank four but did not meet semantic, alignment, or causal-necessity criteria.
A late residual shared-access representation aligned across independently initialized agents and supported reports, joint planning, and flexible tasks.
Direct ablation selectively damaged shared outputs while preserving private routines.
A one-sided patch transmitted to the partner in one round but was corrected by persistent local evidence on return.
Same-rank PCA performed comparably, so Jacobian specificity is not established.
Message-only communication solved the immediate task and therefore is not itself evidence of shared workspace closure.
